key_insight: MonoArt decouples object structure from motion by progressively reasoning about part decomposition and then estimating articulation, allowing stable monocular reconstruction of articulated 3D objects without multi-view or retrieval-heavy pipelines.
problem_solved: How to reliably infer geometry, part structure, and motion parameters of articulated objects from a single image despite the entanglement of motion cues and object structure that destabilizes direct articulation regression.
method: Progressive structural reasoning: incrementally infer a hierarchical part decomposition and refine part geometry before estimating joint parameters.
Alternating structure-and-motion estimation: use structure-aware priors and differentiable assembly to disentangle articulation from shape, improving stability of pose regression from one view.
Single-image training with structural regularizers and targeted losses (e.g., part consistency, kinematic plausibility) to avoid reliance on multi-view data, retrieval, or heavy video synthesis.
impact: Enables scalable, efficient monocular articulated 3D reconstruction suitable for AR/animation, robotic perception, and downstream shape-and-motion tasks by reducing dependence on multi-view supervision and expensive retrieval pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: progressive stages from input image -> part decomposition -> joint estimation -> assembled articulated 3D model.
Side-by-side reconstructions: input image, coarse part layout, final articulated 3D mesh (showing pose changes).
Part-graph / kinematic diagram: nodes = parts, edges = joints with axes and DOF visualized to show disentanglement.
Performance charts: accuracy/completeness vs baselines and ablation bars showing benefit of progressive reasoning and structural regularizers.
paper_title: MonoArt: Progressive Structural Reasoning for Monocular Articulated 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Haitian Li, Haozhe Xie, Junxiang Xu, Beichen Wen, Fangzhou Hong
